newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, but with gains pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, but with gains pared.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer in relatively light trading in contrast to Tuesday's fund-led selling, but the market appeared fragile on the highs and lost much of its gains by close, failing once again to stay above 90 cents per pound for the most-active December contract.
Local speculators were trying to push up the market to shake out those who had sold short, but there was not enough interest and they eventually sold off, a large trader said.
The trader said LME stockpiles will grow during October. "A lot of copper was taken off to take advantage of the backwardation, giving the illusion copper was going to consumption," the trader said.
LME stocks have fallen sharply in the past two weeks.
With LME now in contango, much of that metal lent to the market will go back into exchange stocks and push prices significantly lower to 78 to 83 cents per pound, he believed.
Some traders, however, said market direction was less clear, but that copper was due to stay within its current trading range unless there was a big shift in fundamentals.
December COMEX settled 1.25 cents firmer at 89.10 cents per pound, traded 90.10 to 88.20 cents.
U.S. construction spending rebounded in August, up 0.9 percent to an annual rate of $562.1 billion.
In July spending on construction, a major copper end user, fell by a revised 1.1 percent.
